# `std::walk` — declaration reference

Generated source inventory. Linked guides own runtime and semantic contracts; a listed declaration does not establish executable behavior.

[All modules](../README.md) · [Source](../../../stdlib/std/walk.lani#L3)

Layer: `std`. Role: module. Profile: **Source inventory**.

Implemented resumable Linux directory cursor over existing Reader/file-operation bindings. Descriptor-anchored depth-first traversal uses filesystem order, explicit descend/prune decisions and Entry/Enter/Leave/Fault events. Event paths, names and handles borrow cursor state until its next mutation. Recoverable metadata/open/verify/read/close faults remain visible; terminal limits/allocation errors retain owners until explicit close. Close attempts all remaining owners once, frees storage and does not spend traversal budget. Active-reader, entry, path and work bounds are explicit; no snapshot consistency or hostile-namespace sandbox is promised. All five library gates pass: four native groups/60 cases covering events, decisions, limits, filesystem mutation and reached host/allocation faults, plus 39 host observer controls. Migrated text_grep passes both gates/35 cases (23 comparisons and 12 fault runs) on Linux x86_64 CPU output. These finite receipts exclude GPU-device execution, other targets and formal verification.

```lanius
pub fn default_limits() -> Limits
```

Returns 64 active directories, 65,536 entries, 4095 relative-path bytes, 134,217,728 work units and 32,768 reader-buffer bytes.

### function: open

[Source line 65](../../../stdlib/std/walk.lani#L65)

```lanius
pub fn open(root:core::path::Path,limits:Limits) -> Result<Cursor,Error>
```

Opens a root relative to AT_FDCWD and returns one explicit cleanup authority; first traversal event is root Enter.

### function: open_at

[Source line 70](../../../stdlib/std/walk.lani#L70)

```lanius
pub fn open_at(parent_fd:i32,root:core::path::Path,limits:Limits) -> Result<Cursor,Error>
```

Borrows parent_fd and root bytes only for construction, admits metadata/limits/work before host operations, and owns the opened root independently. Construction errors release partial resources.
